description: Build a Confidence Calibration Analyzer that cross-references confidence ratings with correctness to identify misconceptions (high confidence + wrong) and lucky guesses (low confidence + correct). This is critical for CFA prep because misconceptions lead to systematic errors on exam day.
steps: Create src/features/insights/components/confidence-calibration.tsx - a comprehensive client component that: (1) reads all PracticeAttempts and builds a confidence matrix per subject: Mastered (correct+High), Solid (correct+Medium), Lucky Guess (correct+Low), Misconception (wrong+High), Weak Area (wrong+Medium), Knowledge Gap (wrong+Low), (2) displays a 2x3 grid/matrix visualization with counts and percentages, (3) lists the top 20 'Misconception' questions (wrong + high confidence) with full question text, what the user chose, and the correct answer - these are the HIGHEST priority items to study, (4) shows 'Lucky Guesses' as a warning - topics where user got correct but with low confidence need reinforcement.
Add a 'Fix Misconceptions' quick-start button that creates a targeted quiz session from the misconception questions only (mode='WeakTopic', filtered to high-confidence incorrect questions).
Wire the confidence calibration component into the Insights page (insights-content.tsx) as a section between the existing metrics and the topic heatmap.
Run bun run tsc --noEmit to verify.
acceptance_criteria: Confidence matrix shows accurate counts derived from PracticeAttempt data (AttemptQuestion has confidence field)
Misconceptions (high confidence + wrong) are prominently highlighted with full question details
Lucky guesses (low confidence + correct) are shown as areas needing reinforcement
Fix Misconceptions button creates a valid quiz session targeting those specific questions
verification: Run: bun run tsc --noEmit - expect exit 0
Run: bun run vitest --run - expect same or better pass count
